data.summary: services/sessions render_reconstruction prints len(state.lessons) as 'Lessons carried forward' and _rc_knowledge only skips non-live bullets; with only retired lessons it prints the intro with no bullets. Count and the 'No lessons' fallback should use live lessons. Found by reviewer qwen3.8 on the SZ-split-sessions move (pre-existing code, not changed by the split).
data.title: replay brief counts retired lessons as carried forward

data.summary: services/sessions _recorded_recently only rejects events OLDER than the window; capture_prompt passes now=fired_at which can precede an earlier hook's record ts, so a record in the 'future' counts as recent and a legitimately second prompt is dropped as duplicate. Needs an absolute-distance or lower-bound test. Reviewer finding (qwen3.8), unverified by repro; pre-existing code, not changed by the split.
data.title: capture_prompt drops a later hook's prompt as duplicate when an earlier slow hook wrote after its fired_at

chunk_findings.detail: `render_reconstruction` reports `Lessons carried forward: len(state.lessons)` (all lessons), while `_rc_knowledge` only emits bullets for lessons with `ls.live` and only prints the `_No lessons were recorded._` fallback when `state.lessons` is completely empty. Given a state with one lesson whose `live` flag is false, the generated brief says one lesson is carried forward, then under “Standing knowledge — read before starting” prints the “These were learned the hard way…” introduction but no lesson bullets; with a mix of live and retired lessons, the count is also larger than the rendered list. The count and the “no lessons” fallback should be based on live lessons, because retired lessons are not carried forward or intended to be read before starting.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_reconstruct.py:_rc_knowledge

chunk_findings.detail: `_recorded_recently` only excludes events whose age is *greater* than the window, so a matching event whose timestamp is later than the supplied `now` is treated as recent. `capture_prompt` calls it with `now=fired_at`, and `fired_at` can be earlier than the timestamp of a prompt written by a slower earlier hook. Example: with `DOUBLE_FIRE_S=3` and `HOOK_START_MAX_S=30`, hook A fires at `t=0` and writes its `session.prompt` at `t=20`. Hook B fires the same session with the same text at `t=10` (outside the 3-second double-fire window, so it should be recorded) and calls `capture_prompt` at `t=21`. The code sets `fired=10`, sees A’s event with `ts=20`, computes an age that is not greater than 3 (negative if `clock.age_s` is signed, zero if it clamps future ages), and returns `"duplicate"`, dropping the second prompt. The predicate needs a lower bound/absolute window, or `capture_prompt` must not compare record timestamps against a fired time that can precede those records.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:_recorded_recently / capture_prompt

chunk_findings.detail: The lazy re-export changes the semantics of monkeypatching the old `sessions` namespace. In the old single-file module, code such as `mock.patch.object(ddflow.services.sessions, "redactor", fake)` made internal callers like `capture_prompt`/`note` use `fake`, because those callers resolved `redactor` in the same module. In the new package, those callers live in `_record` and resolve `_record.redactor`; the package-level `sessions.redactor` is only an alias installed lazily in `__init__`. The patch is therefore silently ineffective, so redaction still uses the real `redactor`. This is observable input/interleaving that the stated “no behaviour change” forbids; the modified test in the manifest is a symptom of this regression rather than a change without behavioral effect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/__init__.py:_SUBMODULE_OF / `_reexport.reexport`

chunk_findings.detail: `render_reconstruction` reports `Lessons carried forward: {len(state.lessons)}` using the raw size of `state.lessons`, but `_rc_knowledge` filters with `if not ls.live: continue`. If `state.lessons` contains only retired lessons (`live=False`), the summary says “Lessons carried forward: 1” and `_rc_knowledge` still prints “These were learned the hard way…” while emitting no lesson bullet points, so the reconstruction brief both overcounts carried-forward lessons and produces an empty “Standing knowledge” section that falsely claims there are lessons to read. The count and the branch condition should both filter for live lessons.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_reconstruct.py:46

chunk_findings.detail: `end` writes the caller-supplied `summary` directly to the committed event log with `log.append("session.ended", session_id, {"summary": summary})` and never passes it through `redact`. Given `end(log, "s-1", summary="api key sk-1234")`, the raw secret is committed in plaintext forever, while the same text in `prompt`/`note` would be redacted. The module’s security contract is that text is redacted on the way into the committed log, so this is a leak.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:end

chunk_findings.detail: The guard `if _age_s(ev.ts, now) > window: continue` never rejects a negative age, so a `session.prompt` whose timestamp is after `now` is always treated as inside the window. `capture_prompt` passes `now=fired`, which can be earlier than an existing same-text prompt’s append timestamp when that prompt is written while the current hook invocation is still delayed. Example: existing same-subject text is appended at t=10, current invocation has `fired_at` t=5 and reaches the call at t=15; `_age_s` returns -5, which is not `> 3`, so `_recorded_recently` returns True and `capture_prompt` returns `"duplicate"` even though the firings are outside `DOUBLE_FIRE_S` and the prompt should have been recorded. Real repeated prompts can be silently lost.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:_recorded_recently

data.command: [REDACTED:path] -m ddflow review SZ-split-sessions --gate critic --intent 'Pure move: split services/sessions.py into a package; no behaviour change.'

chunk_findings.detail: The split is not behaviour-preserving for the package’s public namespace. In the old single module, `start` and `new_session_id` shared one module dictionary, so rebinding the public dependency through the package changed what `start` used: `ddflow.services.sessions.new_session_id = lambda cfg, used: "s-fixed"` made `ddflow.services.sessions.start(log, cfg)` return `"s-fixed"`. After the move, `start` lives in `ddflow.services.sessions._record` and still resolves `new_session_id` from `_record`’s globals, while `__init__.py` only re-exports the name in the package namespace. Thus the same assignment to `ddflow.services.sessions.new_session_id` leaves `sessions.start(log, cfg)` minting a real session id, silently changing behaviour for any caller or test that patched the public dependency through `ddflow.services.sessions`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:start

chunk_findings.detail: The lazy re-export dictionary makes `sessions.redactor` (and every other mapped name) a read-only view of the submodule global, but assignment to the package attribute does not propagate to the submodule that actually executes the code. After this change, `import ddflow.services.sessions as sessions; sessions.redactor = fake; sessions.capture_prompt(...)` binds `fake` only in `sessions.__dict__`; `_record.capture_prompt` still resolves `redactor` in `_record.__dict__`, so the real redactor is used. In the old single module, the same assignment mutated the global namespace used by `capture_prompt`, so monkeypatching `ddflow.services.sessions.redactor` (or constants such as `DOUBLE_FIRE_S`) worked. The modified `test_redact_provider_keys.py` shows that patching the old module attribute was an existing pattern; any remaining test or caller that still patches `sessions.<name>` will now silently test/use the real implementation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/__init__.py:67

chunk_findings.detail: `_recorded_recently` only rejects events whose age is greater than the window, so it treats events with timestamps after the supplied `now` as recent. `capture_prompt` passes `now=fired`, where `fired` can be in the past (it is clamped to `now - HOOK_START_MAX_S`). Given current time `T`, an existing `session.prompt` with the same cleaned text at `T-10`, and a call to `capture_prompt(..., fired_at=T-60)`, the code computes `fired=T-30`; `_age_s(T-10, T-30)` is negative or zero, so it is not greater than `DOUBLE_FIRE_S=3`, and `capture_prompt` returns `"duplicate"` without recording the prompt. The intended double-fire window is 3 seconds, but a stale `fired_at` can suppress matching prompts recorded up to about `HOOK_START_MAX_S` before the current call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:_recorded_recently / capture_prompt

chunk_findings.detail: `plan_adoptions` chooses the nearest session by raw string comparison of `e.ts` values, but the same file explicitly says ISO timestamps can appear with or without fractional seconds. Given events with a start `old` at `2023-12-31T23:59:59.000000Z`, a start `new` at `2024-01-01T00:00:00Z`, and an orphan prompt at `2024-01-01T00:00:00.500000Z`, the `new` start is chronologically before the orphan, but the string comparison `"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" <= "2024-01-01T00:00:00.500000Z"` is false because `'Z' > '.'`. The orphan is therefore assigned to `old` instead of `new`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:plan_adoptions

chunk_findings.detail: The split changes observable monkeypatching behavior: before the change, `redact` and `redactor` were globals in the same module, so replacing the public attribute `ddflow.services.sessions.redactor` affected calls to `ddflow.services.sessions.redact`. After the move, `redact.__globals__` is the private submodule `ddflow.services.sessions._record`, so the public package attribute `sessions.redactor` is no longer consulted by `sessions.redact`. The updated test itself proves the regression by patching `S._record.redactor` instead of `S.redactor`. Thus existing code or tests that do `monkeypatch.setattr(sessions, "redactor", boom)` and then call `sessions.redact(...)` will silently use the old `redactor`, which is a behavior change contrary to the stated pure-move intent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_redact_provider_keys.py:92

chunk_findings.detail: `render_reconstruction` reports `Lessons carried forward: {len(state.lessons)}`, but `_rc_knowledge` later skips every non-live lesson with `if not ls.live: continue`. For a state containing a retired/dead lesson, the brief’s summary overstates the lessons it actually carries forward; if all lessons are dead, the “Standing knowledge” section still prints the “These were learned the hard way…” preamble but lists no lessons. The count should also filter on `ls.live`, or the section should state that the recorded lessons are not live.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_reconstruct.py:46

chunk_findings.detail: The change to patch `S._record.redactor` instead of `S.redactor` accepts a behavior change. Before the split, replacing the package/module attribute `S.redactor` made `S.redact` call the replacement, because `redact` and `redactor` lived in the same module. After the split, `S.redact` is the function defined in `_record.py`, so it reads `_record.redactor`; assigning `S.redactor` only changes the package-level re-export and is ignored. Given the old supported monkeypatch input `S.redactor = boom` then `S.redact(f"key {key}", cfg)`, the new code no longer returns `RE.FAILED_MARKER`, contradicting the stated “no behaviour change”. The updated test hides this regression by patching the new private submodule instead of preserving the public package seam.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_redact_provider_keys.py:92

chunk_findings.detail: The entire module `ddflow/services/sessions.py` has been deleted (788 lines removed) and split into a package. However, no `__all__` list is defined in `ddflow/services/sessions/__init__.py`, nor are any of the functions (`redact`, `start`, `resolve`, `replay`, `render_reconstruction`, `verify`, `bundle`, etc.) imported or re-exported from the new package `ddflow/services/sessions`. Any external module importing functions directly from `ddflow.services.sessions` (such as `from ddflow.services.sessions import redact, start`) will now raise an `ImportError` because the package namespace does not expose them.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions.py

chunk_findings.detail: `end(log, sid, summary="AKIA...")` appends a `session.ended` event with the `summary` written verbatim: the function neither takes `cfg` nor calls `redact`, unlike `prompt`, `note`, and `capture_prompt`. Because the event log is committed and `replay` renders `session.ended` summaries, any operator-supplied secret or sensitive note passed to `end` is leaked permanently into the log and reconstruction brief, violating the module’s stated redaction-on-write invariant.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:end

chunk_findings.detail: `render_reconstruction` summarizes `- Lessons carried forward: {len(state.lessons)}` while `_rc_knowledge` only emits lessons with `ls.live` true. Given a State whose `state.lessons` contains a retired lesson (`live=False`), the brief reports one lesson carried forward, but the “Standing knowledge” section omits that lesson; if it is the only lesson, the section still prints the “learned the hard way” introduction with no bullets instead of indicating there are no standing lessons. This gives a rebuild agent a wrong lesson count and a misleading knowledge section.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_reconstruct.py:43

chunk_findings.detail: `harness_session_id` returns `""` for any non-empty harness id that `safe_filename(raw, repl="", max=48)` reduces to nothing (for example `"///"` and `"////"`), because `if not safe: return ""` executes before the collision digest. The docstring says this maps a harness’s own id to one ddflow session per conversation and that sanitising collisions should be separated by a digest. With the empty return, `capture_prompt` falls back through `sid = harness_session_id(harness_id) or resolve(...)`, so two distinct harness ids that sanitize to empty resolve to the same latest/implicit session; `resolve` also ignores such harness env vars and may attach notes/prompts to an unrelated open session. This can mix conversations and make double-fire dedupe (`subject=sid`) suppress one conversation’s prompt as a duplicate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:harness_session_id

chunk_findings.detail: `render_reconstruction` says `Lessons carried forward: {len(state.lessons)}`, but the later `_rc_knowledge` section only lists lessons with `ls.live`. If `state.lessons` contains a retired/superseded lesson (`live=False`), the brief’s summary overstates how many lessons are actually carried forward and contradicts the “Standing knowledge” section. Concrete input: one live lesson plus one non-live lesson produces a summary line `Lessons carried forward: 2` while only the live lesson is listed in the standing-knowledge section.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_reconstruct.py:46 render_reconstruction

chunk_findings.detail: `harness_session_id` is not injective. For example, `harness_session_id("a/b")` produces `h-ab-<D>` where `<D> = content_digest("a/b", length=16)`. But `harness_session_id("ab-<D>")` also returns `h-ab-<D>`, because `safe_filename` leaves `ab-<D>` unchanged and the function then skips the digest. Two distinct harness conversation IDs therefore map to the same ddflow session id, so prompts from different conversations can be merged into one session log.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:harness_session_id

chunk_findings.detail: `plan_adoptions` sorts and compares timestamps as raw strings (`starts = sorted((e.ts, e.subject) ...)` and `ts <= o.ts`). Timestamps can have mixed ISO-8601 shapes, as `_age_s` explicitly supports no-fractional-second forms, and lexicographic order is not chronological: `"10:00:00.500000Z"` sorts before `"10:00:00Z"`, even though `.5` is later than `.0`. With starts at A=`10:00:00.500000Z`, B=`10:00:00Z`, and an orphan at `10:00:00.200000Z`, chronological nearest-previous is B, but the string comparison puts A first and B greater than the orphan; `before` is empty, so it picks A, the session that actually starts after the orphan. `adopt_orphans` then writes the orphan copy under the wrong session.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:plan_adoptions

chunk_findings.detail: The renderer table is missing the `"upgrade.progress"` entry even though `_rs_upgrade_progress` is defined exactly for that event kind (its docstring: "A run's progress record (`status` started, step or failed)"). In `replay()`, an event with `ev.kind == "upgrade.progress"` passes the `PROVENANCE_KINDS` filter, but `_REPLAY_RENDERERS.get(ev.kind, lambda _n, _e: None)` returns `None`, so the step is silently dropped. For example, `replay([Event(kind="upgrade.progress", data={"run": "r1", "status": "started", "items": ["a"]})])` returns `[]` instead of the `ReplayStep` that `_rs_upgrade_progress` would produce, changing reconstruction output despite the supposed pure move.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_replay.py:_REPLAY_RENDERERS

data.summary: services/sessions plan_adoptions uses 'ts <= o.ts' on raw strings; '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z' <= '2024-01-01T00:00:00.500000Z' is False because 'Z' > '.', so the orphan is adopted by an earlier session. _age_s already parses any ISO shape. Reviewer finding (qwen3.8, critic) on SZ-split-sessions; pre-existing, unchanged by the split.
